questions.question: Where should hazardous materials shipping papers NOT be kept?

options.text: In a pouch on the driver's door.
In a pouch on the passenger's door.
Within the driver's reach while wearing a seat belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a pouch on the passenger's door.
questions.explanation: Shipping papers must be easy to access in an emergency. Keep papers in a pouch on the driver's door or within immediate reach while the seat belt is fastened. You can keep them on the driver's seat when the driver is not in the vehicle.

questions.question: If "Inhalation Hazard" appears on a shipping paper, what placard must the shipper provide?

options.text: Poison Gas or Poison Inhalation Hazard

questions.correctAnswerText: Poison Gas or Poison Inhalation Hazard
questions.explanation: When "Inhalation Hazard" appears on the shipping paper or package, display the "Poison Inhalation Hazard" or "Poison Gas" placard as appropriate.

questions.question: How often must hazardous materials employees be trained and tested?
questions.explanation: All drivers must receive training on the security risks of hazardous materials. This includes recognizing and responding to security threats. Training and testing must happen at least once every three years.

questions.question: What is the minimum fire extinguisher rating required on a placarded vehicle?
questions.explanation: A placarded vehicle must have a fire extinguisher with an Underwriters Laboratories (UL) rating of 10 B:C or higher.

questions.question: What shape are hazardous materials placards?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: What is the symbol for a marine pollutant?

options.text: A bird in a red octagon
A fish in a white triangle with an X through it
A light blue square with a dark blue X through it

questions.correctAnswerText: A fish in a white triangle with an X through it
questions.explanation: The marine pollutant symbol shows a fish in a white triangle with an X through it.

questions.question: When can an improperly placarded vehicle be moved?

options.text: To make room for other vehicles.

questions.explanation: An improperly placarded vehicle may only be moved if necessary to protect life or property in an emergency.

questions.question: What should you do to the engine before loading or unloading flammable liquids?
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before loading or unloading flammable liquids, unless you need the engine running to operate a pump.

questions.question: How should a shipper warn others about hazardous materials?

options.text: By posting HazMat placards on the truck.
By putting flashing lights on the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: By posting HazMat placards on the truck.
questions.explanation: Shippers must display diamond-shaped warning signs (placards) on vehicles carrying hazardous materials. Shippers must also provide labels, shipping papers, and emergency response information.

questions.question: Why do shippers package hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: Shippers package hazardous materials to completely contain them. Vehicles must be placarded to show the risk of the cargo.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1 explosives, you must park at least ____ away from any building.
questions.explanation: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, do not park within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, building, place where people gather, or open fire.

questions.question: Who can transport hazardous materials?

options.text: A driver with a CDL and hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver with a CDL and hazardous materials endorsement.
questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle that carries hazardous materials.

questions.question: How must hazardous material containers be prepared?

options.text: Secured so they do not move during transport.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured so they do not move during transport.
questions.explanation: Containers must be braced so they will not fall, slide, or bounce around during transport.

questions.question: What do you do if a hazardous materials label will not fit on the package?

options.text: Place the label on a tag firmly attached to the package.
Attach a QR code to be scanned.
Make the label smaller so it fits on the package.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place the label on a tag firmly attached to the package.
questions.explanation: If a label does not fit on the package, attach it to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.

questions.question: Many poisonous products are also:
questions.explanation: Many poisonous hazardous materials are also flammable.

questions.question: When can you leave a vehicle carrying explosives unattended?

options.text: On the side of a highway.

questions.explanation: You may leave your vehicle unattended only in a safe haven. A safe haven is an approved location for parking unattended vehicles loaded with explosives.

questions.question: What license does a driver need to transport hazardous materials?

options.text: A CDL with hazardous materials endorsement.
A CDL with a tank endorsement.

questions.correctAnswerText: A CDL with hazardous materials endorsement.
questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle that carries hazardous materials.

questions.question: Who is responsible for labeling hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for packaging, marking, and labeling hazardous materials and providing warning placards.

questions.question: Where can you find identification numbers for chemicals?

options.text: In the DOT Emergency Response Guide.
In the Periodic Table of Elements.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the DOT Emergency Response Guide.
questions.explanation: The DOT Emergency Response Guide (ERG) contains information about hazardous chemicals. It is indexed by proper shipping names and identification numbers.

questions.question: If "G" appears in Column 1 of a hazardous materials shipping paper, what else must be included?

options.text: The technical name of the hazardous material.

questions.correctAnswerText: The technical name of the hazardous material.
questions.explanation: A "G" in Column 1 means a generic name is used. A generic shipping name must include the technical name.

questions.question: Unless a package is clearly unsafe, a driver needs ____ to accept it.
questions.explanation: The shipper certifies that hazardous materials are packaged correctly. You can accept the package based on this certification unless it appears unsafe or does not meet regulations.

questions.question: During a cargo fire, opening the trailer doors may make the fire spread because it:

options.text: Changes the temperature of the trailer.
Provides more moisture to the trailer.

questions.explanation: Opening trailer doors during a cargo fire lets oxygen in. This can cause the fire to grow larger and spread faster.

questions.question: If hazardous materials in your cargo catch fire, you should:

options.text: Try to put out the fire with a fire extinguisher.
Call emergency personnel and let them handle the fire.
Keep driving to the fire department.

questions.correctAnswerText: Call emergency personnel and let them handle the fire.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials fires need special training and equipment to fight safely. Call emergency personnel and let them deal with the fire.

questions.question: Hazardous materials shipping papers should be:

options.text: Kept in a pouch attached to the driver's side door.
Taped to the passenger's side window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Kept in a pouch attached to the driver's side door.
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's side door. They must be easy to reach while wearing a seat belt and easy to see for anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: After an accident with hazardous materials, which is NOT your job as a driver?

options.text: Keeping people away from the scene.
Trying to put out the fire yourself.
Telling emergency personnel about the hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Trying to put out the fire yourself.
questions.explanation: Your job is to keep people away, tell emergency personnel about the hazards, and give them the shipping papers. Do not fight the fire yourself unless you have proper training and equipment.

questions.question: Class 1, Class 2.1, and Class 3 materials should not be placed in a trailer with:
questions.explanation: Do not use heaters in the same space when transporting Class 1 (Explosives), Class 2.1 (Flammable Gases), or Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) materials.

questions.question: Hazardous materials placards are usually which shape?
questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying hazardous materials must display diamond-shaped warning signs on all four sides. These signs are called placards.

questions.question: A driver should make sure that:

options.text: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on packages.
The shipping paper is written in code.
All packages are labeled as poison.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on packages.
questions.explanation: Compare the markings and labels on packages to the shipping papers. Make sure the shipper has the correct description on the paper and the correct labels on the packages.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, do not park your vehicle:
questions.explanation: Never park a vehicle with Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building. Only brief stops for vehicle operation are allowed.

questions.question: If an explosives package has an oily stain or is damp, the driver should:

options.text: Use towels to absorb the liquid.

questions.explanation: Never transport damaged explosives packages. Do not accept any package that appears damp or has an oily stain.
